title: Sterivex RNA Extraction Protocol
author: Ariel Rabines
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bd9ti96n

steps.title: Prepare Lysis Buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare the Lysis Buffer for N samples (plus extra for pipetting) and X quantity of internal standard mix (usually 1-2.5 μL).

substeps.instruction: In a sterile container, add 800 µL x N of Lysis Buffer MR1.
Add 14 µL x N TCEP.
Add X x N μL of internal standard mix.
Mix well.
Add 750 µL of RNase-free H2O to the TCEP vial.
Incubate for several minutes at room temperature.
Mix the vial to dissolve TCEP completely.
Store dissolved TCEP at -20 °C.
Add 800 µL of RNase-free H2O to the rDNase vials.
Incubate for 1 min at room temperature.
Gently swirl to completely dissolve (do not mix vigorously).
Store at -20 °C for up to 6 months (do not freeze/thaw more than three times).

steps.title: Prepare rDNase Reaction Mixture
steps.instruction: Prepare the rDNase reaction mixture based on the quantity needed from the epMotion program.

substeps.instruction: Gently mix at a ratio of 276 µL Reaction Buffer for rDNase to 24 µL rDNase working solution.

steps.title: Load Sterivex Filters
steps.instruction: Load the prepared sample volume into Sterivex filters, keeping the filters on dry ice.

substeps.instruction: Remove the luer plug from each Sterivex.
Pipette the per sample volume (e.g., 815 µL if using 800 µL MR1 + 14 µL TCEP + 1 µL internal standards) into each.
Dispense quickly to prevent lysis buffer from freezing upon contact.
Replug with luer lock.
Place luer-side down into a 1.5 mL tube rack.

steps.title: Incubate and Vortex Samples
steps.instruction: Incubate and mechanically agitate the samples.

substeps.instruction: Incubate at 33 °C and shake gently for 00:10:00.
Vortex for 00:05:00 using an adapter for 5 mL tubes.

steps.title: Extract Lysate from Sterivex
steps.instruction: Recover the lysate from the Sterivex units into labeled 1.5 mL sterile tubes.

substeps.instruction: Label each Sterivex with its extraction number.
Use tube cutters to pop the lid off the end of the Sterivex by applying pressure at an upward angle in the lip between the lid and the unit; cut around the top if needed.
Rub the filter on the inside of the Sterivex to release as much lysis buffer and material as possible.
Pipette as much liquid as possible from inside the Sterivex into the corresponding 1.5 mL tube.

steps.title: Clear Lysate by Centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate to clear it.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 5600 x g for 6 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare Beads and Binding Buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare the bead mixture during centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Premix beads and Binding Buffer MR2 at a ratio of 28 µL beads : 772 µL MR2.

steps.title: Isolate Supernatant
steps.instruction: Transfer the cleared lysate to a new set of numbered 1.5 mL tubes.

substeps.instruction: Remove as much supernatant as possible without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Transfer to Deep Well Plate
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to a deep well plate.

substeps.instruction: Align 1.5 mL tubes in rack in plate position.
Set an adjustable spacer multichannel pipette to 800 µL.
Transfer no more than 800 µL into the deep well plate.

steps.title: Run epMotion Program
steps.instruction: Process the deep well plate using the epMotion system, eluting into a twin.tec LoBind PCR plate.

substeps.instruction: Set up reservoir rack layout (left to right): MR2 with beads, MR3, MR4, MR4, MR5, MR2 without beads, DNase.
Run the program.
At Step 4, stop the program.
Use a P1000 multichannel pipette to thoroughly pipette up and down to mix the bead solution.
Continue the run.

steps.title: Quantify and Analyze RNA
steps.instruction: Perform quantification and quality control on the eluted RNA.

substeps.instruction: Create a 1:10 dilution plate (20 µL total volume) using elution buffer MR5 (RNase-free H2O).
Quantify the dilution plate with RiboGreen assay to calculate original concentration and total RNA.
Analyze 1 µL on Agilent Tapestation with RNA screentape.
